body:
It seems that the SW is stripping headers (and other "metadata") from requests (e.g. [here][1] and other places as well). This is intentional (to a degree) to avoid things like credential inclusion in order _"to avoid issues with opaque responses"_.

We might be over-aggressive here (e.g. it might be OK to preserve (some) headers).
@alxhub should know more about what kinds of issues we are trying to avoid and if we can be less aggressive.

[1]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/2d9111bfb698aa1e418cbd73b33e3ef73209084e/packages/service-worker/worker/src/assets.ts#L145-L148
Any updates on that? Working with the service worker is great, but with this "bug" not so production ready....
I am quite surprised that this feature has not been fixed, almost a year later. Should we start using Workbox instead?

# 🐞 bug report

### Affected Package
ngsw-worker.js

### Is this a regression?
No

### Description
We are trying to use the service worker to cache resources pulled from an S3 bucket.  However, we receive CORS errors which prevents the resources from loading.  When the service worker is disabled, the fetching of the resources works fine.

Note that my CORS policy on the s3 bucket is set to allow all origins, which is confirmed by the fact it works when the service worker is disabled.

I have done some debugging of the code and found that when new requests are objects are created in the service worker, that the new request's mode is set to "cors" whereas the original ones are "no-cors".  For example, this line:

                    const res = yield this.fetchAndCacheOnce(this.adapter.newRequest(req.url));

console.log(req.mode); // outputs no-cors
console.log(this.adapter.newRequest(req.url)); //outputs cors

I'm not sure if it's related, but that's where am in triage.

## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction

https://github.com/byronlbailey/swissue
1) Clone the repo to local workstation
2) ng build --prod
3) cd dist/swissue
4) http-server (may need to install this npm module)
5) open incognito browser to url specified by http-server
6) The image may show the first, time, but after refreshing your browser it typically disappears

## 🔥 Exception or Error
`Access to fetch at 'https://eksplor.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/game/diamondlakes1/main.png' from origin 'http://127.0.0.1:8081' has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource. If an opaque response serves your needs, set the request's mode to 'no-cors' to fetch the resource with CORS disabled.
The FetchEvent for "https://eksplor.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/game/diamondlakes1/main.png" resulted in a network error response: the promise was rejected.
Promise.then (async)

    at LazyAssetGroup.<anonymous> (ngsw-worker.js:662)
    at Generator.next (<anonymous>)
    at fulfilled (ngsw-worker.js:196)`
